winning_patterns: Short 13-15 second clips with high-energy streamer reactions outperform longer 30 second clips, as seen in the 370 median views for shorts versus 284 for medium clips.
Hooks using all-caps promises or specific game-breaking events like crashing or physics bugs drive significantly higher views than generic gameplay descriptions.
YouTube Shorts is the dominant traffic driver for top performers, with GTA-001 earning 9400 of its 10410 views from YouTube alone.
avoid_patterns: Reject clips with typos or broken English in hooks such as 'MASSAGGATOR BC CRASH' which resulted in zero views across all platforms.
Avoid generic 30 second 'reaction' clips without a specific payoff, as demonstrated by GTA-019 and GTA-008 earning under 600 views.
Do not post clips with zero engagement metrics or zero views across TikTok and Instagram, as seen with GTA-027 and GTA-028.
hook_style_guidance: Write Frame-1 hooks in all-caps that promise a specific, high-stakes failure or glitch involving the streamer's name to trigger immediate curiosity.
